cards.back: ① clear attribute **semantics** ② reduce **redundancy**/update anomalies ③ reduce **NULLs** ④ disallow **spurious tuples**.
**Insertion** (can't add a row without unrelated key data), **Deletion** (lose data when removing the last row), **Modification** (redundant copies → inconsistency). Motivation for normalization.
**Bottom-up (synthesis)** = build from attribute relationships (impractical). **Top-down (analysis)** = start from natural groupings, decompose. FD theory supports top-down.
Join only on **(PK, FK)** pairs. Joining on non-key common attributes produces **spurious tuples** (lossy join). The lossless-join property prevents them.
For any two tuples, **t1[X]=t2[X] ⟹ t1[Y]=t2[Y]**. X functionally determines Y. A semantic constraint on all legal states.

cards.front: Can you prove an FD from one state?
cards.back: **No.** A state can only **disprove** (rule out) an FD via a counterexample (equal X, different Y). FDs come from meaning, not from one instance.
**Superkey** = uniquely identifies (may have extras). **Candidate key** = minimal superkey. **Prime** attr = in some candidate key; **non-prime** = in none.
**Full**: removing any LHS attribute breaks it. **Partial**: a non-prime attr depends on **part** of a (composite) key → **2NF killer**.
key → (non-prime) → (non-prime), i.e. X→Y→Z with the middle non-prime → **3NF killer**. (If middle Y is a candidate key, it's fine.)
**Trivial**: Y ⊆ X (holds always). **MVD X↠Y**: for each X, the set of Y values is independent of the rest (Z=R−XY) → defines 4NF.
**IR1 Reflexive** (Y⊆X ⟹ X→Y), **IR2 Augmentation** (X→Y ⟹ XZ→YZ), **IR3 Transitive** (X→Y, Y→Z ⟹ X→Z). **Sound + complete.**
**Decomposition** (X→YZ ⟹ X→Y, X→Z), **Union** (X→Y, X→Z ⟹ X→YZ, *same LHS*), **Pseudo-transitivity** (X→Y, WY→Z ⟹ WX→Z).
Split/combine **RHS** freely. **Never split LHS**: XY→A does NOT give X→A; X→A & Y→B does NOT give XY→AB. Union needs the **same** LHS.
Start with X; repeatedly add the RHS of any FD whose LHS ⊆ X⁺, until stable. **X⁺ = R ⟹ X is a superkey.** X→Y holds iff Y ⊆ X⁺.
All FDs implied by F (apply Armstrong repeatedly). Up to **2^(2^n)** possible FDs for n attributes — so we use closures/covers instead of listing it.
① test if X is a **superkey** (X⁺=R), ② test if **X→Y holds** (Y⊆X⁺), ③ build blocks for **candidate keys**, **equivalence**, and **minimal cover**.
**F covers E** if every FD of E ∈ F⁺. **F ≡ G** (equivalent) iff F covers G **AND** G covers F (E⁺=F⁺). Test: closures **both ways**.
For each X→Y in **G**, compute X⁺ **using F** and check Y ⊆ X⁺. If all pass, F covers G.
① single attribute on **RHS** ② no **extraneous LHS** attribute ③ no **redundant FD**. A smallest set equivalent to F.
**1)** split RHS (canonical) → **2)** remove extraneous LHS attrs → **3)** remove redundant FDs. Use the **current reduced set** for each closure check.
**No.** Different reduction orders give different (equivalent) minimal covers. Say '*a* minimal cover', not '*the*'.
**Essential** attr = on the **RHS of no FD** → in **every** candidate key. Compute closure of essentials; if = R it's the only CK, else add non-essentials.
Single candidate key of size **x**, **n** total attrs → **# superkeys = 2^(n−x)** (the remaining n−x attrs are each in/out). e.g. n=6, x=2 → 16.
K := R; for each attr A, if (K−A)⁺ = R then K := K−A. Returns **one** key (order-dependent). Use essential-attrs for **all** keys.
**Normalization** = decompose to remove redundancy/anomalies. **Denormalization** = re-add redundancy *after* normalizing for read speed (cost: harder updates, inconsistency).
Every attribute is **atomic** — no composite, multivalued, or nested attributes. Fix multivalued → one row per value; fix nested → split tables propagating the PK.
1NF **+ no partial dependency** (every non-prime attr fully depends on the **whole** key). Only matters when the key is **composite**.
2NF **+ no transitive dependency** of a non-prime attr on the key (no key → non-prime → non-prime). Decompose EMP_DEPT → ED1 + ED2.
For every X→A: **X is a superkey OR A is a prime attribute**. The 'A prime' clause is what BCNF removes.
Depend on **the key** (1NF), **the whole key** (2NF — no partial), **and nothing but the key** (3NF — no transitive).
For every FD X→A, **X must be a superkey** (no 'A is prime' escape). Strictly stronger than 3NF: 1NF⊃2NF⊃3NF⊃BCNF.

cards.front: When is a relation 3NF but not BCNF?
cards.back: Exactly when some **X→A has X not a superkey and A a prime attribute**. Classic: **TEACH** {Student,Course}→Instructor, Instructor→Course.
Violating FD X→A: decompose into **(R−A)** and **(X∪A)**, repeat. **Any 2-attribute relation is always in BCNF.**
**Lossless (non-additive) join** — must ALWAYS hold (no spurious tuples). **Dependency preservation** — desirable, achievable only up to **3NF** (BCNF+ may lose FDs).
{R1,R2} lossless iff **(R1∩R2)→(R1−R2)** OR **(R1∩R2)→(R2−R1)** ∈ F⁺ — the shared attrs must be a **key of at least one** piece.
If forced to choose, **lossless join wins** — a lossy decomposition corrupts data. Losing dependency preservation only means a constraint needs a join to check.
**MVD X↠Y**: Y values independent of the rest for each X. **4NF**: every nontrivial MVD has a **superkey** determinant. Fix: split (X,Y) and (X,Z).
**JD(R1..Rn)**: R = R1⋈...⋈Rn losslessly. **MVD = JD with n=2.** **5NF**: every JD component is a superkey. Rare (JDs hard to detect).
1NF (atomic) → 2NF (no partial) → 3NF (no transitive) → BCNF (every determinant superkey) → 4NF (MVD superkey) → 5NF (JD superkey). Each strictly stronger.
**Scanner** (tokens) → **Parser** (syntax) → **Validation** (names) → **query tree/DAG** → **Optimizer** (plan) → **code gen** → **runtime execution**.
**Semi-join** (EXISTS/IN): return left row at **first match**. **Anti-join** (NOT EXISTS/NOT IN): return left row **only if no match**. Engines unnest subqueries into these.
**S1 Linear** (always), **S2 Binary** (ordered key), **S3a Primary index** / **S3b Hash** (equality, ≤1 record), **S4 Index range** (>,<,≥,≤ on ordered key).
**J1 Nested-loop** O(m·n); **J2 Index nested-loop**; **J3 Sort-merge** O(m+n) after sort; **J4 Partition-hash** (partition into buckets, probe matching ones).
Missing/unused indexes, **SELECT *,** complex joins/subqueries, **functions in WHERE** (block indexes), large unfiltered scans.
Use **indexes**, select **only needed columns**, optimize **joins**, **filter early with WHERE**, use **LIMIT**. Goal: touch fewer rows/columns sooner.
**EXPLAIN** shows the plan (access order, indexes). A **B-tree index** turns a SELECT from full scan **O(n)** into lookup **O(log n)**; costs storage + slower writes.
An attribute removable from an FD without changing F⁺. Test: if (X−B)⁺ (using the rest of F) still contains A, then B is extraneous in X→A.

cards.front: Ruling out an FD from data
cards.back: For candidate X→Y, scan row-pairs with equal X: if any differ on Y, the FD is **ruled out**. Data can disprove but never prove an FD.
EMP_PROJ(Ssn,Pnumber,Hours,Ename,Pname,Plocation), PK={Ssn,Pnumber}: split into **EP1(Ssn,Pnumber,Hours)**, **EP2(Ssn,Ename)**, **EP3(Pnumber,Pname,Plocation)**.
TEACH(Student,Course,Instructor), Instructor→Course violates BCNF → decompose into **(Instructor,Course)** + **(Instructor,Student)** (D3, the only lossless one). Loses fd1.
REFRIG(M,Y,P,MP,C), F={M→MP, MY→P, MP→C}: essential M,Y; **MY⁺ = R** ⟹ CK = MY. (M→MP and MP→C violate BCNF/3NF.)
'α→β and γ→β ⟹ α→γ' is **NOT sound** — two determinants of β needn't determine each other. Verify rules via Armstrong or a counterexample.
F={A→C,AC→D,E→AD,E→H}, G={A→CD,E→AH}: A⁺={A,C,D}, E⁺={A,C,D,E,H} under **both** sets ⟹ F covers G and G covers F ⟹ **F = G**.
**Forbidden:** prime → non-prime → **non-prime** (transitive on key). **Allowed:** chain ending in a **prime** attribute (3NF escape clause b).
**Spurious tuples** (lossy join — shared col not a key) and **lost dependencies** (an FD spans two pieces). Losslessness is mandatory; dependency-preservation desirable.
SQL is split into **query blocks** (one SELECT-FROM-WHERE [+GROUP BY/HAVING]); each block → extended relational algebra (query tree) → optimized independently.
